newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria says Netanyahu must honour commitments.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Netanyahu must honour commitments.

text.p: Syria said on Thursday it would not agree to fresh talks with Israel until Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accepted all the understandings reached with the Jewish state's previous government.
The Syrian position was spelled out in the official press after the United States said it had formulated with Israel proposals for renewing peace talks with Damascus.

"Netanyahu is ready to negotiate without committing himself to withdrawal from the Golan. The previous agreements and understandings do not bind his government. He doesn't want to resume the talks from the point where they stopped but from the zero point," the official daily al-Thawra newspaper said.
"Syria will never be dragged into such traps. No force could ever push Syria to what it doesn't want and to what contradicts its national rights and the land-for-peace principle," the newspaper said.
Syria has maintained in five years of sporadic talks that only a full Israel withdrawal from the Golan Heights captured in the 1967 Middle East war would open the door to peace.
Netanyahu, who ousted Labour party leader Shimon Peres in a national election last May, wants to keep the strategic plateau in Israeli hands.

He has called on Syria to renew talks unconditionally, although a report on Israel's Channel Two television said on Wednesday Netanyahu was ready to accept some of the understandings reached by the government he toppled.

Peres and slain prime minister Yitzhak Rabin had agreed in talks with Arab partners to the principle of exchanging land for peace but said the extent of Israel's withdrawal depended on Syria's readiness for normalisation.

U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Wednesday after talks between Netanyahu and U.S. leaders that Washington and Israel had developed proposals for restarting peace talks with Syria, suspended since March.
He said the proposals had been passed on to Damascus.
Burns said U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross had long talks on the subject with Dore Gold, a key adviser to Netanyahu, after the Israeli leader met President Bill Clinton on Monday.
Ross may travel to the Middle East next week, U.S. officials said.
